belief: A loving God wouldn't let me suffer like this.
origins: Pain makes God’s love hard to see. If He is all-powerful and loving, the logic seems to say He would stop it. Many faithful people have struggled with this tension.
teaches: “My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways My ways.” Habakkuk, Job, and the psalmists asked why. “Why, O LORD, do You stand far off?” God’s love is shown most clearly in the cross: “God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” “We do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses.” Not all questions have answers now, but God is with you, and suffering does not disprove love.
self_statements: If God loved me, He would stop it.
He could help but does not.
Love would not let this happen.
Either He is not loving or not powerful.
I do not understand His love.
errors: Believing God is either loving or lets me suffer.
Feeling pain and concluding that God does not love me.
questions: What exactly do I feel God has done or failed to do?
Where did the psalmists take such questions?
What did God do about suffering at the cross?
Who has shown me God’s love in this?
What can I know even if I do not understand?
What would it look like to bring this honestly to God?
truth: Suffering does not prove that God does not love me. His love was shown at the cross. I can ask my hardest questions, and He can bear them. I can trust Him even without all the answers.
hw_truths: God proved His love at the cross.
His ways are higher than mine.
log: Each week, write one honest prayer.
actions: Tell God exactly what you think.
Talk to a pastor or friend.
prayer: Lord, I do not understand why. Hear my honest questions, show me Your love, and hold me until I see more. Amen.
